title: DeepSeek-R1 dialogue leads a 34-year-old man to a genetically confirmed familial Mediterranean fever diagnosis after roughly three decades of symptoms
summary: Patient's DeepSeek-R1 dialogue proposed FMF; MEFV genetic testing confirmed it and colchicine stopped attacks after ~30 years of symptoms.
account: A 34-year-old man of Egyptian origin with recurrent fever, migratory abdominal pain, arthralgia, myalgia and erythematous skin lesions since early childhood began a dialogue with the DeepSeek-R1-0528 model on 28 June 2025. The model refined its differential toward familial Mediterranean fever and recommended specialist evaluation, inflammatory markers, genetic testing and colchicine under supervision. He arranged genetic testing, which found two pathogenic MEFV variants (p.Met694Val and p.Val726Ala), and obtained colchicine 0.5 mg twice daily from an Egyptian pharmacy; his attacks ceased, but alanine aminotransferase rose to 160 U/L. Colchicine was temporarily discontinued, his liver enzymes were monitored by his primary care physician, and after they improved it was resumed at 0.5 mg daily under close supervision. He presented to the Department of Medicine III, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, Germany, in February 2026, already taking 0.5 mg daily; the clinic confirmed FMF and he has remained attack-free.
purpose: DeepSeek-R1 is a general-purpose reasoning chatbot; answering a user's medical questions with a differential diagnosis falls within its general question-answering function, though it is not a validated medical device.
segment: Patient-initiated use of a consumer LLM
taxonomy_note: Closest fit: the patient obtained a correct diagnostic hypothesis outside the health system after decades without one. The authors also document harm from unsupervised self-medication (ALT 160 U/L), which the depth rating takes into account.

ratings.reason: Inflammatory attacks that had recurred since early childhood ceased on colchicine after a genetically confirmed diagnosis; the benefit is life-changing, tempered by a documented transaminase rise from self-dosing before medical supervision.

ai_role.statement: The LLM generated the FMF hypothesis and the suggested work-up over a multi-turn dialogue; confirmation came from MEFV genotyping and clinical response to colchicine. The authors stress that the model repeatedly advised specialist supervision and that the self-directed genetic testing and self-medication were the patient's own actions.
